mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 220 or 230 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a C220 or C230 petrol typically costs between £500 and £4,500 depending on the engine code and condition. Used M111 units start from £500-£1,300, reconditioned from £1,200-£2,400, and fully rebuilt M272 V6 engines from £2,200-£4,200. Labour for supply & fit adds £500-£1,000.

mainEntity.name: What is the balance shaft failure on the M272 V6 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early M272 engines (serial numbers below 2729..30 468993, 2004-2008) suffer from balance shaft sprocket wear due to soft metal being used in the manufacturing process of the timing gear. This causes the timing to be thrown off, triggering fault codes P0016/P0017 and potentially leading to costly engine damage if not addressed. Repair costs at a specialist are approximately £2,200-£3,500 for balance shaft and timing chain replacement.

mainEntity.name: Does the C-Class 220 or 230 petrol have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: All C220 and C230 petrol engines use timing chains, not belts. The M111 (W202), M271 (W203) and M272 (W203/W204) all use timing chains. However, the M271 is known for timing chain stretch (60k-100k miles), and the M272 is known for balance shaft sprocket wear affecting timing accuracy. A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign for timing chain issues.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain problems in a C-Class 220 or 230 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: On M271-equipped models (W203 C230 Kompressor), the most common symptom is a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start. Other signs include the check engine light (P0017 code), rough idle, loss of power, extended cranking, and hard starting. On M272-equipped models (W203/W204 C230 V6), codes P0016/P0017 indicate balance shaft sprocket wear.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 220 or 230 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W202 C220 or C230 is typically worth £1,000-£3,000 - a full engine replacement often exceeds the car's value, making a used engine or targeted repair more economical. A W203 C230 Kompressor is worth £2,000-£5,000 - a rebuilt M271 engine (£2,000-£3,500) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. A W203/W204 C230 V6 is worth £2,500-£6,000 - a rebuilt M272 engine (£2,200-£4,200) is usually within the car's value.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the M271 and M272 engines in the C230?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M271 is a 1.8-litre supercharged four-cylinder engine used in the W203 C230 Kompressor (2000-2005), producing 163 hp with a timing chain. The M272 is a 2.5-litre naturally aspirated V6 engine used in the W203 and W204 C230 (2005-2009), producing 204 hp. The M272 offers more power and refinement but has the balance shaft sprocket weakness. The M271 is more prone to timing chain stretch.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 220 / 230 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The C220 and C230 petrol badges span multiple generations of the Mercedes-Benz C-Class, representing the mid-range petrol options. The C220 was offered in the W202 generation with a 2.2-litre four-cylinder M111 engine. The C230 badge evolved from a 2.3-litre four-cylinder in the W202 to a 1.8-litre supercharged four-cylinder in the W203, and finally to a 2.5-litre V6 M272 in the W203 and W204 generations - offering a smooth, refined alternative to the four-cylinder range.

milestones.description: M111.961, 2.2L four-cylinder petrol, 148 hp - W202 C220 launch; DOHC 16-valve; 210 Nm torque
M111.975, 2.3L four-cylinder petrol, 148 hp - W202 C230 launch; same power output as C220 but larger displacement
M271.948, 1.8L supercharged petrol, 163 hp - W203 C230 Kompressor launch; Eaton M45 supercharger; 230 Nm torque
M272.920, 2.5L V6 petrol, 204 hp - W203 C230 launch; 245 Nm torque; 90° V6 architecture
M272.921, 2.5L V6 petrol, 204 hp - W204 C230 launch; 245 Nm torque; continued V6 offering
W204 C230 production ends; replaced by C250 CGI four-cylinder

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 220 / 230 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The C220 and C230 petrol have been powered by three distinct engine families - the M111 (W202), the M271 (W203) and the M272 (W203/W204). The M111 is robust but suffers from head gasket and camshaft sensor issues. The M271 is notorious for timing chain stretch. The M272 V6 has a well-documented balance shaft sprocket weakness. Rebuilt C220 and C230 petrol engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components designed to address the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: M271 Timing Chain & Camshaft Adjuster Failure
problems.h4: M271 Timing Chain & Camshaft Adjuster Failure - The W203 C230 Kompressor Weakness
problems.rootCause: The M271 uses a single-row timing chain that stretches prematurely, often combined with failing camshaft adjusters (phasers). Symptoms include a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start. P0017 almost always points to a stretched timing chain or a failing camshaft adjuster. The M271 engine is an interference design - if the timing chain breaks or slips, valves and pistons hit and the engine is effectively junk.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, both camshaft adjusters
repairOptions.longevity: Best done at first rattle; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Cylinder head removal, valve replacement, piston inspection, full timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has slipped; bent valves almost certain

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement with professionally rebuilt M271 unit with upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Best long-term value on higher-mileage cars

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W203 C230 Kompressor is worth £2,000-£5,000. For vehicles under £3,500, a preventative chain replacement (£1,100-£1,800) is usually the better financial decision than a full engine replacement. For higher-value examples, a rebuilt M271 with warranty (£2,500-£4,200) offers peace of mind.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold starts - especially between 60,000 and 100,000 miles - act immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist (£1,100-£1,800) saves thousands compared to waiting for failure.

problems.h4: M272 Balance Shaft Sprocket Wear - The V6's Critical Weakness
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 230 (M272.920 and M272.921, W203 and W204, 2005-2009)
problems.rootCause: Early M272 engines (serial numbers below 2729..30 468993, 2004-2008) suffer from balance shaft sprocket wear due to soft metal being used in the manufacturing process of the timing gear. This causes the timing to be thrown off, triggering fault codes P0016/P0017 and potentially leading to costly engine damage if not addressed. The balance shaft in the early M272 V6 engines was known to have problems due to soft metal being used in the manufacturing process of the timing gear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace balance shaft with updated sprocket, timing chain, tensioner, guides
repairOptions.longevity: Required if caught early; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full engine rebuild with new balance shaft, timing components, cylinder head work
repairOptions.longevity: Required if timing has jumped or engine damage has occurred

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete replacement with professionally rebuilt M272 unit featuring upgraded balance shaft and timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Best long-term value; ensures all weak points addressed

problems.recommendation: If your W203 or W204 C230 V6 throws codes P0016/P0017 and you have an early M272 engine (serial below 2729..30 468993), the balance shaft sprocket is almost certainly the cause. A balance shaft and timing chain replacement at a specialist (£2,200-£3,500) is the most cost-effective solution. On a C Class worth £2,500-£6,000, if the engine has already suffered damage, a fully rebuilt M272 with upgraded components may be the better long-term investment.
